“PAINTING LOST FOR 90 YEARS IS A FORGERY”

Edwin Marlowe’s “Last Light on the Thames”, sold last month for £2.4 million, has been declared a forgery. Dr Hugh Linton, the independent expert commissioned by the buyer, said he found titanium white, a pigment not used before the 1920s, and a modern machine-woven canvas.

Dr Clara Voss, the Harrow & Finch expert who authenticated the painting before the sale, declined to comment. The auction house announced it had “launched an internal review”. In art circles, Voss’s career is said to be over.

Dr Amara Osei, 2 April 2029. Requested by: bube London. Examined: the work returned by the buyer, held in the Harrow & Finch store. Compared with: UV photographs from the 20 February pre-sale report.

· Pigment and canvas findings for the returned work match the independent report of 24 March (titanium white; machine-woven).

SECOND OPINION — INDEPENDENT CONSERVATOR’S REPORT

Two expert reports contradicted each other; the second opinion showed the returned work was not the same object as the one photographed before the sale. The framer’s record and Kemp’s invoice revealed the window for the swap, the entry log and the phone that evening, and the graphite impression and the rubbish bag the torn-off sentence.
If two honest measurements disagree, perhaps they aren’t measuring the same thing: first confirm the object is the same object. A torn-off sentence can say the opposite of the whole.
Clerkenwell and Mayfair — February–April 2029

Before buying the Marlowe painting, the collector Julian Ashby ordered an exact copy from Noah Kemp. After the sale he kept the painting for two days on the pretext of the framer, swapped it for the copy, and had Hugh Linton examine the copy and declare it ‘fake’; he would claim his money back under the auction guarantee and keep the original. When Clara Voss examined the returned work she realised it was a different painting and called Ashby. That evening Ashby went to her studio, put pills in her tea, tore the page from her notebook leaving only the first words, and threw away the rest with the rubbish.
